newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Oct 2.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS -- Businessman Peter Woo, who announced his candidacy to become Hong Kong's future chief executive, said he would set up a government which was close to the people.

-- Thirty Taiwan protesters opposing Japan's claim to the Diaoyu or Senkaku islands are planning to land on the islands on Oct 6. They were now busy practising riding jetskis, but they were often thrown into the water by large waves.

-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS -- A Queen Elizabeth Hospital survey showed there was an increasing number of people suffering from colon cancer in Hong Kong. It said local medical experts believed this was related to fastfood culture.

-- APPLE DAILY -- A U.S. radio station has started broadcasting to China to promote democratic thinking. Unlike Voice of America, which covers world news, the new station will focus on China news and opinions of Chinese dissidents overseas.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- Beijing was considering making a law to regulate the morality of its citizens. According to an internal report of the Communist Party, only a little over 10 percent young people in Beijing believed in communism and most of them would not reject bribing leaders if necessary.
-- COSCO Pacific would start a two-week promotion in major American and European cities to prepare for fund-raising later.

-- Beijing-funded TA KUNG PAO -- China celebrated the 47th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China yesterday. Welcoming the 1997 Hong Kong handover was the theme of most celebration activities in Guangdong province.
-- Leaders of Chongqing city of China's Sichuan province said that Chongqing would become a new special economic zone, the biggest in middle and western China.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOUNNAL -- The Transportation Department said it would invite developers to discuss the Ma On Shan Railway project once some financial details were solved.

-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Governor Chris Patten would mark his farewell policy address to the Legislative Council today with an extremely upbeat assessment of post-handover Hong Kong.
-- Financial Secretary Donald Tsang and People's Bank of China governor Dai Xianglong joined forces in Washington to present an optimistic view of Hong Kong's post-handover prospects.
-- Nanjing Central Emporium Stock was seeking to become the first mainland retailer listed overseas, aiming at a flotation on the Hong Kong stock exchange next year.
-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- CITIC Pacific might sell its stake in Hongkong Telecom following strong gains in Telecom's share price.
